subject: Custom SLA: low-latency guarantee & burst-tolerance carveout request
messages:
From: Amelia Soto <amelia.soto@soteriahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@soteriahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Request: low-latency guarantee + burst tolerance carveout for Soteria pilot

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move the pilot into production, but two procurement asks came up during the security/procurement sync:

1) A firm 95th percentile latency commitment for inference calls at 16k context (SLO target: <= 120ms across EU region).
2) A documented carveout that allows for controlled burst tolerance during nightly batch ingest windows (we need an exception path so we aren’t penalized during scheduled data pushes).

Attached is our standard procurement PO and a short doc with the proposed SLA annex language (SLA_Annex_Soteria_v1.docx). Can Redwood commit to a custom addendum with specific latency numbers and a defined burst-tolerance clause? If not, what alternative mitigations (regional pinning, dedicated capacity, or queued batch windows) would you recommend to avoid production throttles?

We’re targeting a signed order and activation by Dec 10. Appreciate quick guidance so procurement can complete the legal review.

Best,
Amelia Soto
Head of Platform Operations
Soteria Health

Attachments: Soteria_PO_20261128.pdf (application/pdf), SLA_Annex_Soteria_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Soto <amelia.soto@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: low-latency guarantee + burst tolerance carveout for Soteria pilot

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear ask and the docs. Short answer: we can support a custom SLA addendum, but it will require a couple of things to be explicit in the order form:

- Whether you want the latency commitment on Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant) vs Redwood Dedicated. For a 95th percentile <=120ms at 16k, Dedicated is the most reliable path.
- If Dedicated is not an option, we can offer a hybrid approach: EU-hosted model pinning + regional capacity reservation (burst buckets) and an explicit "scheduled batch window" carveout documented in the annex.

Kimberly — can you confirm if a carveout clause with a scheduled-batch exemption and an operational notification window (~48 hours) is acceptable from a legal/penalty perspective? I’ll loop in Marissa from CS to map out the onboarding runbook so we can set telemetry and evidence for credits if an SLA is breached.

Amelia — I’ll draft proposed language and share by tomorrow. If you can also confirm whether Soteria prefers credits (service credit formula) vs. fee offsets, that helps legal/finance finalize the order form.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: low-latency guarantee + burst tolerance carveout for Soteria pilot

Team —

We can support a scheduled-batch carveout in the SLA annex with conditions:

- The carveout must be narrowly scoped (identified windows, maximum daily-duration) and require 48-hour advance notice for non-emergency scheduled events.
- Any unplanned bursts that exceed the carveout will be evaluated against telemetry; credits only apply if behavior meets the "service-affecting" criteria defined in the main SLA.
- For a 95th <=120ms at 16k, we strongly prefer Dedicated capacity with a minimum reservation term (3 months) to make the commitment contractual. If Soteria cannot do Dedicated, we can add regional pinning + burst buckets but the service-credit bands will be wider.

I will draft annex text with both options (Dedicated + Hybrid) and mark the carveout parameters. Karthik / Marissa — can you estimate operational lift for Dedicated provisioning vs configuring burst buckets in EU? I need the numbers to justify the legal language.

-Kimberly
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: low-latency guarantee + burst tolerance carveout for Soteria pilot

Jonas / team —

Operational detail: provisioning Dedicated EU pool (8 GPUs, estimated) to hit 95th <=120ms at 16k would take ~7 business days after order + capacity planning. Runbook work: prefix/KV caching config, model quantization at 4-bit where acceptable, and a pre-roll performance test. Cost uplift estimate: ~35% above comparable hosted rate for reserved capacity (we can provide a line-item in the order form).

Hybrid option: regional pinning + burst buckets is faster (2–3 business days) but we can only guarantee a softer SLO (95th <=160ms) and define a burst bucket that limits daily burst minutes. Credits under hybrid are smaller in scale.

I’ll include a short ops appendix for the annex that enumerates telemetry tags we’ll use for evidence (route id, model id, instance id, region).

-Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Soto <amelia.soto@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: low-latency guarantee + burst tolerance carveout for Soteria pilot

Amelia —

Thanks for the quick review. Summary / next steps: 

1) Redwood can deliver a custom SLA addendum. Two options in the draft annex: Dedicated (recommended) — 95th <=120ms at 16k; Hybrid — 95th <=160ms with defined burst bucket.
2) Kimberly will send draft legal text for both options by EOD.
3) Marissa will attach the ops appendix and cost uplift line item for Dedicated vs Hybrid.
4) Please confirm which option Soteria prefers (Dedicated or Hybrid) and whether you want credits or fee-offsets as the primary remedy. Also confirm acceptance of the PO attachment so we can route to Finance.

If we get a go/no-go by Dec 3 we can meet your Dec 10 activation target. Linking the draft DocuSign here: https://app.redwood.example/docusign/abc123

Cheers,
Jonas
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
